discovery.md:148: 'On a repo without that file, fall back to the portable core in `references/patterns.md`.' — establishing patterns.md as the authoritative id set for no-rubric repos
advisory.finding: The discovery.md `antipattern_id` field spec enumerates only three portable ids in its 'otherwise' clause (`fixture-mutates-foreign-state`, `mismatched-hardening-equivalence`, `unstated-policy-oracle`), but references/patterns.md — the designated fallback for a repo without code-review-tests.md — defines FOUR portable ids, additionally including `fail-open-oracle`. A finding produced in a no-rubric repo for a fail-open oracle has an admissible `antipattern_id` in patterns.md that the discovery.md schema field's enumeration does not permit, exactly the two-halves-disagree drift concern #12 was added to catch.
scenarios: A discovery subagent runs concern #12 on a repository that lacks src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md, finds a fail-open oracle, and must pick an antipattern_id per the discovery.md schema field, which does not list fail-open-oracle.
advisory.suggested_fix: In discovery.md's `antipattern_id` field, note that when falling back to patterns.md its four portable ids apply (including `fail-open-oracle`), or explicitly state fail-open-oracle is owned by code-review-tests.md and therefore excluded from the portable 'otherwise' set only when that rubric is present.
